verdict.rationale: Kino documents one user-configurable background behavior: a saved filter becomes a smart bin that fills automatically as footage arrives. It also says cloud agents can install Kino and edit while you're away, but that autonomy comes from third-party agents, and no general automation builder, recurring schedule, or trigger-action rules are documented. A community user also wanted reusable formats so an agent could produce recurring episodes from a few commands, which suggests repeatable workflow automation is not yet there. Missing for 10: a general automation or workflow builder, recurring scheduled runs, event triggers beyond smart bins, first-party background agent execution, and independent hands-on corroboration of unattended runs.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Save a filter and it becomes a smart bin that fills as footage arrives.
Cloud agents like Dot, Muse, Grok Bot and Devin install Kino on their own computer and edit while you’re away.
